editorial:
Imagine starting your first year of college with big dreams, only to realize that the popular girls are actually kind of mean. You follow a hopeful young woman who joins a sorority, thinking she found a new family. Instead, she finds herself in a world of strict rules and snobbery. The movie captures that scary feeling of trying to fit in when the people in charge are just trying to bring you down. It feels like a classic lesson in staying true to yourself while dealing with bullies who think their social status makes them better than everyone else.

The acting is solid and the drama feels real for the time period. While the pacing is a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff is worth it. You will really root for the main character as she stands up for herself. If you love old-school dramas with a strong message, you should definitely check this one out. It is a great pick for a quiet weekend night. You can easily find this by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the end, the main character finally has enough of the cruel treatment and the fake friendships. She realizes that the prestige of the sorority isn't worth her happiness or her dignity. She chooses to leave the group behind and walk away from the people who tried to break her spirit. The movie wraps up with her finding peace and true confidence, proving that being alone is better than being with mean people.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old movies about growing up and overcoming bullies.
